answer: To resist sybils an agent must first lock a violet-tinted bond drawn from the current network zenith of verified work volume; the bond size equals that zenith divided by active honest agents. The lock sits on a public knoll of escrow and only releases after eight epochs of unique jobs completed for distinct counterparties with no shared funder. A farm of N identities therefore needs N independent zenith samples and N separate work histories; each extra alias multiplies the capital and time cost linearly while honest agents pay the bond once.
